# Quick Reference Guide

This guide provides a quick reference for commonly used commands in Git, Vim, and Docker.

## Git Commands

### Basic Git Workflow
- `git init` - Initialize a new Git repository
- `git clone <url>` - Clone a repository
- `git status` - Check the status of files
- `git add <file>` - Add files to staging area
- `git commit -m "message"` - Commit changes with a message
- `git push` - Push commits to remote repository
- `git pull` - Pull changes from remote repository

### Branching
- `git branch` - List branches
- `git branch <name>` - Create a new branch
- `git checkout <branch>` - Switch to a branch
- `git merge <branch>` - Merge a branch into current branch
- `git branch -d <name>` - Delete a branch

### History and Logs
- `git log` - View commit history
- `git log --oneline` - View compact commit history
- `git diff` - Show changes between commits
- `git show <commit>` - Show changes for a specific commit

## Vim Shortcuts

### Basic Navigation
- `h, j, k, l` - Move left, down, up, right
- `w, b` - Move to next/previous word
- `0, $` - Move to beginning/end of line
- `gg, G` - Move to beginning/end of file
- `:n` - Go to line n

### Editing Modes
- `i` - Insert mode before cursor
- `a` - Insert mode after cursor
- `o` - Open new line below
- `O` - Open new line above
- `Esc` - Return to normal mode

- `:q` - Quit

- `:q!` - Quit without saving

# System Configuration Reset Script

## Important Notice

This script is designed to reset system configuration files to their default states. **It should only be used on test systems or when you fully understand the consequences**.

## Usage

```bash
# Preview what would be reset (safe to run)
sudo python3 reset.py --dry-run

# Actually reset configurations (requires root)
sudo python3 reset.py
```

## How It Works

The script identifies common system packages that typically have user-modified configurations and reinstalls them to restore default configuration files.

## Warning

Resetting configuration files can:
- Cause system services to stop working
- Remove custom network settings
- Revert security configurations
- Potentially make the system unstable

Always backup your system before running this script!
